description: Freehand fallback after insert_* feature tools. part_id is required and must be the active part's opaque surf id (a vault path or display name is unknown_part; another id is part_mismatch). Writes that part, runs it, and records one undo step when the text changes. Working copy only: nothing reaches git without an explicit git_save. Preserves or re-injects `// @surf-id`. Keep the feature marker blocks (// --- <kind> begin --- … // --- <kind> end ---, and // @contour id=) so the strip keeps per-feature edit, delete, rollback and undo; see guide { topic: "features" }. Do not declare a reserved SurfCAD helper name with const, let, class, or function — the runtime passes these as function parameters: addDraft, align, array3D, booleanBodies, boundaryEdges, cboreHole, center, chamferEdges, clearanceHole, concaveEdges, convexEdges, cskHole, cut, deleteFace, draftFaces, edge, edgesBetween, edgesByOrientation, edgesOf, externalBody, faceNames, facesByNormal, facesNamed, fastenerClearanceDia, fastenerMajorDia, fastenerTapDrillDia, filletAlongPath, filletEdges, getDimensions, getScaleRatio, hexPrism, hole, holePattern, holeSpan, holesOnContour, hollow, listFastenerSizes, loft, makeCrossSection, makeExtrude, makeLoft, makeRevolve, makeSweepPath, mirror, move, moveFace, offsetPlaneFrame, patternOnPoints, placeInFrame, placeOnFace, planarFaceAt, polarArray, profileCircle, profilePolygon, profileRectangle, rectTube, resolveFastenerSize, rotateAbout, rotateContour, roundedBox, sheetMetalSolid, shell, signedFeatureEdges, solveContour, sumSqDist, surfaceOf, sweep, sweepPoints, tapDrillHole, transformByFrame, tube, vecAdd, vecCross, vecDot, vecMul, vecNorm, vecNormalize, vecSub, workplaneFromFace. A redeclaration fails; rename your variable (for example `const cut`). list_helpers { names } (over MCP) or guide { topic: "dialect" } documents each helper. Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

part_id.description: Part id to write. Must match the active part. Not a vault path.

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

source.description: Script text written into the editor and run.

name: set_script
